content.comment_body: Hello! I want to manage 4 light outputs and measure how long each has been on. When the fourth output turns on, I would like to turn off the one that has been on the longest. I'm having trouble comparing four timers to find the largest value.
It's difficult to assist without details about which controller and software you are using. Could you provide more information?
Sorry, you are right! I'm using a new [product_name] with [product_name].
There still isn't enough information. Do all timers have the same values? Have you already written a program?
The timers have different values, representing how long each output has been on. I don’t have a program yet, and I’m not sure where to start.
It is possible to compare several activation durations to determine which is the longest. However, without a program or complete functional details, it's difficult for me to help further.
The attached document shows inputs that activate independently. I would like to determine which input has the longest activation period.
Check the attachment. For testing, the time base of the timers is set in seconds.
This is an excellent solution—thank you very much!
Hi, I'm trying to replicate this, but when I download your example, the parameter selection for the Analog Mux is greyed out. I'm using [product_name] [version_no].
This is normal because starting from [article_no], referencing is set up using reference lines instead of entering block numbers in the parameter fields.
Sorry if this seems basic, but do you mean the connections to the function block when you refer to reference lines?

Just to clarify, by reference lines, do you mean the wires connected to the function block? In the screenshot, the green line is a reference line—it connects the output of the analog amplifier to the parameter V1 of the math instruction block. In this example, the properties show B001 for B002, which is why the parameter field is greyed out in B002.
